title: Zayin
hookLine: the letter that begins zachor, remember

cards: A puzzle hiding in plain sight. The Ten Commandments appear in Exodus, and then again, when Moses retells them, in Deuteronomy. Side by side, they're nearly the same.
But the Sabbath commandment opens with a different word in each. In Exodus it's zachor: remember. In Deuteronomy, it's shamor: keep, guard, observe.
Which one did the people hear at the mountain? The rabbis had an answer, and you can still hear it sung on Friday nights.

teach.b: First, the word it opens. Zachor, remember. In the King James: "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy."
The very first sound of that command is a zayin. So is the first sound of zikaron, a memory, and zecher, a remembrance. Second, the other word.
Deuteronomy opens with shamor, to guard or observe. Remember is something you do inside. Guard is something you do with your hands and your calendar.
Two verbs, one day. Third, the rabbis' answer.
In the Talmud, in tractate Shevuot, they say God spoke both words at once, in a single utterance, something no human mouth could do.

Much later, a poet put that teaching into Lecha Dodi, the song congregations sing on Friday evening to welcome the Sabbath. One of its lines says it outright: keep and remember, in one word. The puzzle became a song.
Fourth, why remembering gets its own commandment.
In this tradition, memory isn't just what happens to you.
It's something you do on purpose. The prayer for the dead said on certain festivals is called Yizkor, may God remember.
Zayin turns the past into a task: not waiting for a memory to arrive, but choosing to call someone to mind.

how: Congregations welcome the Sabbath on Friday evening by singing Lecha Dodi, whose verses include the teaching that 'keep' and 'remember' were spoken as one; the kiddush over wine on Friday night also speaks of the Sabbath as a remembrance.

games.q: Exodus says remember the Sabbath. Deuteronomy says keep it. you're a rabbi asked which one was said at the mountain. what does the Talmud answer?
o: keep: Deuteronomy is the later word.
both, spoken as one word at once.

practice: Choose something to remember instead of waiting for it to drift in: a person who taught you something, a morning when things went right, a kindness someone did for you and has probably forgotten.
Bring it back slowly, where you were, what it sounded like, what they said, and stay with each detail as it arrives. If you pray, hold that memory in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Zayin. The letter that begins zachor, remember, and the family of remembering words: zikaron, zecher, Yizkor. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: remember, the first word of the Sabbath command in Exodus 20:8. It begins with zayin (ז).

carryVoice: Your line: zayin remembers. Memory can be something you choose. Go gently.
